title.narrative: Integrated education, health, nutrition, WASH and protection response to IDPs in Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, and Tigray regions

description.narrative: In Abi Adi Central Tigray, enrolment rates are 68% for boys and 78% for girls, but 29% of school-aged children are out of school, exposing them to risks. There are 33,530 school-aged children in the area, with 17,484 being IDPs. Class sizes average 80 children, with a severe shortage of teaching materials and qualified educators, creating a challenging learning environment. The education component supports 8,000 children by providing access to formal and non-formal education, implementing accelerated learning for out-of-school children, and linking these efforts to child protection services. UNICEF will create safe classrooms with adequate WASH facilities, provide teaching materials and train educators in inclusive practices. Ethiopia is currently experiencing a severe cholera outbreak that began in August 2022, and it is still ongoing. From 01 January 2024 to 04 November 2024, there have been 26,497 recorded cases, resulting in 259 deaths and a Case-Fatality Rate of 0.98%. The outbreak is now under control in 85% of the 230 affected woredas, with active cases remaining in only 33 woredas. Over 90% of the cases come from five regions, i.e., Amhara: 27.3%, Oromia: 27.3%, - Afar: 15.2%, Tigray: 12.1% and Benishangul Gumuz: 9.1%. In response, the health component will pre-position Cholera Treatment Centre kits to provide life-saving support for new outbreaks in the country and advocate for sustainable health and WASH investments. UNICEF will collaborate closely with the Ethiopian Public Health Institute, relevant regional health bureaux, the health cluster and other humanitarian partners. This partnership will focus on rapidly mobilizing CTCs and implementing life-saving case management interventions alongside WASH initiatives, Social Behavioural Change, and Risk Communication and Community Engagement efforts to enhance the response.A recent ICCG assessment in August 2024 revealed alarming global acute malnutrition rates in Alamata, Raya Alamata, Korem, Ofla, Zata, and Chercher, ranging from 34% to 48%, with Zata at 48%. Additionally, 72% to 80% of pregnant and breastfeeding women were malnourished, highlighting a critical nutrition crisis. While UNICEF has secured funding for essential nutrition supplies, programming cost gaps remain. The nutrition component will provide life-saving interventions in Oromia, Tigray, and Amhara, including training health workers, providing preventive and curative services, and distributing nutrition supplies.UNICEF will facilitate case management, school admissions, and awareness programs to empower children and caregivers in Tigray. Key activities include case management, family reunification, mental health support, and strengthening community response structures. Additionally, UNICEF will address negative coping mechanisms like child marriage and provide explosive ordnance risk education. This intervention will empower children and caregivers in Tigray through proactive child protection and community engagement. Key activities include case management, family reunification, community-based mental health support, and strengthening community response structures. Additionally, UNICEF will address negative coping mechanisms like child marriage and provide explosive ordnance risk education.UNICEF will procure and distribute essential NFIs for cholera prevention, including water purification chemicals, High Test Hypochlorite/Calcium Hypochlorite, body soap, and laundry soap. These items will support Infection Prevention and Control in Cholera Treatment Centers, Treatment Units, and healthcare facilities. Additionally, 50 communal water systems serving around 75,000 people in cholera-affected regions will be rehabilitated and chlorinated. Regional water bureaux will also receive support for monitoring water quality as part of the cholera response efforts.
